title: Present Tense
logline: Michael calls an unnecessary all-hands that spirals, then finds the one useful thing he can do: getting Jim back to Scranton, while Pam ends her engagement to Roy and answers Jim's card in person.
outline: A: Michael calls a mandatory finale all-hands, fights Toby's Rule Fourteen, then phones Jim to come back; Pam ends the engagement with Roy on the loading dock, and Jim walks in. Michael returns the paintings. B: Dwight and Andy team up to present Pruitt on the Monday Corporate call, for Michael. C: Stanley stuck at 187 with Creed; a rumor goes around like telephone. Order: cold, A, B, A, C, A, B, A, C, A, B, A, tag.
theme: Being present beats being chosen: who you pick matters less than whether you show up.
storySoFar: Season 2 finale. Michael phoned Jim in Stamford and told him to come back to Scranton, giving up his favorite-boss act to let Pam choose. Pam ended her engagement to Roy on the loading dock; Roy walked off, then saw Jim arrive, and is still deciding about June 14. Pam answered Jim's card in person: yes, here. Michael returned the paintings and removed the Michael Scott Collection sign; fun run money goes to the Community Center. Dwight and Andy presented Pruitt as partners to David Wallace and made Michael the voice of Scranton. Stanley is still at 187; Michael's joke died again, and Stanley nodded. Toby's Rule Fourteen stands. Jim's status with Shannon is unresolved. Karen's Stamford hologram exposure is a loose thread.

beats.text: Actually, that's a banjo on hold.

beats.text: One eighty-seven.

scenes.recap: Michael calls a mandatory finale all-hands, and Toby's Rule Fourteen becomes a fight.

beats.text: This meeting is not necessary. But it is important. Sit down, Andy.
My phone's on hold, Michael. It's technically in a meeting.
Rule Fourteen. No banjo during business hours.
Toby, this is my all-hands. Your rule is a footnote.

lines: I'm against banjos during business hours, which is all the hours.

beats.text: One word each. Season two, in one word. Dwight.
Ambitious.
Disappointing.
Dramatic. Amazing dramatic.
Pam?
Honest.

beats.caption: Michael waits for a joke. There is no joke.

scenes.recap: Dwight and Andy agree to share the Monday Pruitt call, for Michael's sake.

beats.text: Monday, three o'clock. David Wallace. You and me, Pruitt, together.
False. You present. I correct. That is the partnership.
Four-minute turns. Cornell debate taught me that.
Question: did the Cornell debate team ever win?
Irrelevant.

lines: Andy and I share Pruitt now. I know the beets. He knows the spreadsheet.
Together we are unstoppable. Separately, I am still better.

beats.text: David said one voice for Scranton. Michael's name is on the hook, Dwight.
Michael is always on the hook. It is his favorite position.
So we do it for him. Not for us.

beats.caption: Dwight considers the offer for three full seconds

beats.text: For Michael. Fine. You get the first four minutes.

scenes.recap: Stanley vents to Creed at the smoking spot, and Creed's Dayton story goes nowhere.

beats.text: One eighty-seven. Still.
In Dayton a wedding judge was a cat. The cat knew everything.
Did I stutter? I'm not asking about Dayton.
The lake froze in June. Nobody asked me about the lake.

beats.caption: Stanley lights a cigarette. He does not ask about the lake.

beats.text: The lake is still there, Stanley. It's always there.
One eighty-seven.

scenes.recap: Michael phones Jim in Stamford and tells him to come back, without telling him what to do.

beats.text: Jim, it's Michael. Don't talk. This is a management call.
Pam is going to say it to you in person. Which means she's serious, which means you should come.
You don't have to be the favorite, Jim. You just have to be in the room.

beats.caption: Michael listens to Stamford breathe

beats.text: Friday. Mandatory Pruitt meeting. Leave Karen in Stamford. Karen makes things a production.

beats.caption: hangs up, then covers his ears with both hands

lines: Pam is my favorite. I'm not supposed to say that. Nobody's supposed to have a favorite.
So I'm letting Jim have her. That's not a bit. That's the nicest thing I've ever done.

scenes.recap: On the Monday Corporate call, Dwight and Andy present together and make Michael the voice of Scranton.

beats.text: 3 P.M. MONDAY: CORPORATE CALL
Dave! Welcome to Scranton. My two number twos are right here.
Who is going to walk me through Pruitt?
Dwight and I. Together.
Andy presents the numbers. I present the reasons.

beats.caption: clicks through a slide titled 'Pruitt, Pruitt, Pruitt'

beats.text: Pruitt is staying?
Question: who would leave Scranton?
Michael, you're still on the hook for the hologram. Who is taking that?
We'll take the hook with him. Michael is the boss, and he's our boss.
Well. Michael, you're the voice of Scranton now.
I'm the voice. They're the spine. It's a whole body, Dave.
I'll allow it.

scenes.recap: Pam ends her engagement to Roy on the loading dock, and Roy walks off to think.

beats.text: Roy, I need to say something, and I want to say it right.
Is it Halpert?
It's not about Jim. It's about me. I'm not happy, Roy. I'm not doing June fourteenth.

Dock's not the problem, man. Asking is.

lines: I bought a binder. The binder has tabs.
Tab one is June fourteenth. Tab two is venues. Tab three I haven't read yet.

beats.text: It's a date, Roy. It's not a promise.
